text: "Man ate angels' food." The Hebrew says "the bread of the mighty," and the manna never touched the ground. It fell on the dew.
explanation:
The word in Psalm 78 isn't the usual word for angels; it's abirim, the mighty. Israel ate champions' food every morning for forty years. And "when the dew fell on the camp in the night, the manna fell on it." It landed on a cushion of dew, a picture of God's favour, never on the dirt.

Jesus said, "Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, and are dead. I am the living bread which came down from heaven; if anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever." The true Bread came down at night in Bethlehem. Feed on Him, and you're eating the food of the mighty.

text: Mankind fell through one act of eating. God has ordained that we eat our way back.
explanation:
If Adam hadn't eaten, there'd be no aging, disease or death; the whole fall came through eating. You aren't born again by taking Communion; that comes by trusting Jesus. But many of the fall's effects (weakness, sickness, depression, decay) can be countered by eating His body and drinking His blood with understanding.

The early church broke bread "from house to house," sometimes many times a day. "Do this in remembrance of Me" is His love language. You don't give your wife a vacuum cleaner on her birthday; you speak her language. Speak His, often.

text: Israel called the manna "this worthless bread," literally "light bread." The Hebrew comes from the word for curse: to make light of.
explanation:
After years of daily bread from heaven, the people complained, "Our soul loathes this worthless bread." The word means making light of something, the opposite of kavod, glory and weightiness. Earlier they'd moaned, "There is nothing at all except this manna before our eyes!" and craved Egypt's fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic.

Those six Egyptian foods all grow on or near the ground; you had to stoop to gather them. The fruit of the promised land hangs at arm's height. When Jesus starts to seem ordinary, when it's "Jesus, Jesus, Jesus again," that's the moment to guard your heart. What you treat as light, you lose the benefit of.

text: Freed prisoners sometimes walk back into their cells because their eyes aren't used to the light. Give your eyes time to adjust.
explanation:
Israel said, "We remember the fish we ate freely in Egypt." Freely? They were slaves. We have short memories about our bondage; we romanticise the past and forget the chains. It's said that when prisoners were freed from dark caves, some went back inside because daylight hurt their eyes.

You can grow so used to an addiction, a depression or a toxic relationship that freedom feels uncomfortable at first. The light may sting before it heals. Stay in it. "If the Son makes you free, you shall be free indeed." And sometimes a disappointment is God's appointment.

text: In the peace offering, the breast went to Aaron and his sons. Our High Priest feeds on His love for us, and we feed on it too.
explanation:
The peace offering (literally "peaces," plural, wholeness in every area) was a voluntary thanksgiving. The fat was burned for God, and "the breast shall be Aaron's and his sons'." The breast speaks of love; the right thigh or shoulder, also given to the priest, speaks of strength. The breast was waved side to side and the shoulder lifted up and down: together, the shape of a cross.

Jesus is our High Priest, and His joy is in loving us. We're His sons, and our food is that same love. John leaned on Jesus' breast. When you read the Word or take Communion, don't just look for promises; feed on how much He loves you.

text: The thanksgiving offering had to be eaten the same day. On the third day it was no longer accepted. Keep your revelation fresh.
explanation:
"The flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offering for thanksgiving shall be eaten the same day it is offered." If any of it was eaten on the third day, "it shall not be accepted, nor shall it be imputed to him." In Greek, thanksgiving is eucharistia, the Eucharist.

Take Communion as though He died just now, not as a distant event two thousand years ago. Last week's chicken rice won't sustain you today, and a revelation you heard years ago won't either. Faith comes by hearing, not having heard. Stay close to the sacrifice and keep coming back for fresh bread.

text: The fuller the head of grain, the lower the stalk bows. A mature believer is a humble one.
explanation:
In a wheat field, the young stalks stand tall and stiff. As the heads fill with grain, they grow heavy and bow toward the ground. The emptiest heads stand straightest.

In the same way, the more of Christ that fills you, the more humble you become. It's those with little inside who need to prove themselves and resent being taught. "God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble. Therefore humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, that He may exalt you in due time."
